title: Say what the slope or intercept means
subtitle: Linear functions · 24 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **24 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 11 Easy, 9 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given a context model, as an equation or a graph with labeled axes, and asked what a coefficient or constant represents.
- The wording is 'each additional', 'per', 'initial', 'at the start', or 'when none'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For 'each' or 'per' questions, the answer is the slope: read the coefficient, or compute rise over run between two clear grid points on the graph.
- 2) For 'initial' or 'starting' questions, the answer is the output when the input is 0, which is the y-intercept.
- 3) Attach the sign and units the question asks for.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: For a given equation, graph it and click the y-intercept, or read the coefficient directly.
For a pictured graph Desmos adds little.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You report the intercept when the slope was asked, or the reverse.
The trap is also that you give a negative rate when the question asks how much is 'used' or 'lost' per unit, which is the magnitude.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
